headline: Auve Tech's driverless electric shuttle has shown it can carry staff and equipment at Tallinn Airport in Estonia with no safety operator on board.
score_reason: Lowered from 5: the authorisation dates from August and what is new is a demonstration; the claims are the company's own.
importance_line: Staff at the airport already ride in vehicles with no one at the wheel or on board, an early example of a driverless service in daily use on private airport roads; the figures and 'first in Europe' claim come from the companies, and the shuttles run between hangars inside the airport area, not on public roads.
summary: Robotics & Automation News reports, from the company's announcement, that the eight-passenger MiCa shuttle, supervised remotely, runs between hangars at Magnetic MRO, an aviation maintenance firm, covering about 1,000 kilometres a week at a stated 99.9 percent autonomy rate, after Auve Tech received authorisation in August 2026 to remove the onboard operator. The company and the airport say it is the first such airport service in Europe, and that one remote supervisor can watch several vehicles, which is what could make driverless transport cheaper.
notes: Day of the August 2026 authorisation not stated, so freshness date is month-only. Airport-area route is read from the article's description of connections between airside hangars.
